texts: A large patch of aortic wall carrying several intercostal arteries can become aneurysmal over time, the big old patch that balloons with the years: D.

The risk is highest when the wall itself is diseased, as in Marfan syndrome, so many surgeons reattach intercostal arteries as small islands or with separate branch grafts, the small button that stays flat.
The artery of Adamkiewicz, the kiwi, usually arises from a left-sided intercostal or lumbar artery between T8 and L1; that segment, not T4 to T7, is the one worth reattaching.
Preserving the blood supply of the spinal cord helps in the repair of atherosclerotic aneurysms too.
Memory hook: the big patch of old skin balloons; the small island stays flat.
